samples.summary: The new peer-rectangle sanitizer validates magnitude but never shape; a malformed presence object crashes every other client's paint loop
samples.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` is introduced as the sanitizer for a peer-written `tableCellRange` ("reaches here verbatim off the wire"), but it only bands the *numbers*: line 139 dereferences `cr.start.rowIndex` / `cr.end.rowIndex` with no check that `start`/`end` are objects. Nothing upstream validates the shape either — `YorkieDocStore.getPresences()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3501) returns `this.doc.getOthersPresences()` cast straight to `DocsPresence`, and `docs-view.tsx:257` copies `sel.anchor`, `sel.focus`, `sel.tableCellRange` verbatim into `PeerCursor.selection`. Attack: an attached collaborator (including a share-link *viewer*, whose presence writes are not gated by the yorkie auth webhook — only PushPull document writes are) sets `activeSelection = { anchor: null, focus: null }` or `{ anchor: a, focus: f, tableCellRange: { blockId: 'x' } }` (no `start`/`end`). On every other participant, `editor.ts:2095` (`peer.selection.anchor.blockId`) or selection.ts:139 throws a TypeError inside `paint()`; `render()` (editor.ts:2395) has no try/catch, so the throw escapes the presence-change/render callback and the canvas stops updating — a one-line presence write from a read-only peer freezes the document for every editor. Since this PR is the code that hardens this exact input, the shape check belongs with the magnitude clamp.

samples.summary: Clamping bounds the rectangle to the table, but the table size is itself peer-chosen and `expandCellRangeForMerges` is an O(area) fixed-point scan run once per paint per peer selection
samples.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` clamps `start`/`end` to the table and then calls `expandCellRangeForMerges(ordered, table)` (line 146), a `while (changed)` loop whose inner `for (r) for (c)` scans the whole rectangle each pass. `normalizeRange` is reached from `computeSelectionRects`, which `editor.ts:2098` calls once per peer per paint (and `getSelectionRects` calls for the local selection). Row count is not banded anywhere — `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (numeric-attrs.ts:95) caps columns at 256 but nothing caps `rows.length` — so a peer who writes a very large table and publishes `tableCellRange` `{start:{0,0}, end:{1e9,1e9}}` gets clamped to the *full table* and then re-scanned each frame, including on paint-only renders where the table layout is not recomputed. `maxCol` additionally reduces over every row on each call. Residual, not introduced: the change also newly routes *nested* tables into this expansion via the `resolveNestedTableLayout` fallback (line 191), widening what reaches it. A cheap fix is to cap the clamped rectangle's area (or the fixed-point pass count) rather than only its indices.
searchedFor: Grep computeSelectionRects call sites in editor.ts

samples.summary: The cycle-guard sweep missed two recursive parent-map walks: `moveToNextCell` / `moveToPrevCell` recurse through `blockParentMap` with no visited set
samples.evidence: This PR adds `seen` guards to six walks over `blockParentMap` on the stated threat model that a peer can write two tables whose ids make the parent chain loop (ids come verbatim from CRDT attributes; the map is built in table-layout.ts:451 keyed on those ids, so duplicate ids across two tables produce A→B and B→A). Two walks over the same map were left unguarded: `moveToNextCell` recurses at text-editor.ts:6007 after moving the caret into the parent cell, and `moveToPrevCell` at text-editor.ts:6065 does the same. With a cyclic map, Tab / Shift+Tab at a table boundary ping-pongs between the two tables until the stack overflows (RangeError out of the key handler) — the same crash the PR closes in `Doc.findBlockInCells`. Confidence is low because the Tab path may pass `addRowAtEnd`, which takes the insert-row branch before the exit branch on the last cell; Shift+Tab (`moveToPrevCell`) has no such branch.

samples.summary: The nesting cap covers the read and layout halves of the structural recursion but not the write serializer or the DOCX importer, which the PR itself names as an untrusted producer
samples.evidence: `table-nesting.ts` and the layout comment (table-layout.ts:136-148) justify the cap by noting the layout "takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste)". Paste is in fact already bounded (`MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8`, clipboard.ts:71), but the write-side mirror of the capped reader — `buildBlockNode` → `buildRowNode` → `buildCellNode` → `buildBlockNode` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364-414) — takes no depth parameter, and `packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts` has no depth constant at all (grep for `depth|MAX_` returns nothing). A hostile .docx with tens of thousands of nested `w:tbl` elements therefore still overflows the stack during import/serialization on the importing client (and in `packages/cli`'s `importDocx`), i.e. the structural-recursion hazard this PR closes on the read path stays open on the ingest path. Impact is limited to the user who opens the file (client-side/CLI only — no server-side import path found), hence minor.
searchedFor: Grep depth|MAX_ in packages/docs/src/import/docx-parser.ts and docx-importer.ts
Grep docx-importer|importDocx|parseDocx across packages (frontend + cli only)

verdict.reason: Verified independently: no shape validation exists anywhere on the peer-presence → paint path, and the crash is unguarded. selection.ts:139-140 dereferences cr.start/cr.end with only numeric clamping (clampCellIndex handles non-finite numbers, not missing objects), and its own doc comment (selection.ts:115-126) states the range arrives verbatim from peer presence. Upstream: yorkie-doc-store.ts:3497-3502 returns getOthersPresences() uncast-checked; docs-view.tsx:244-259 filters only on activeCursorPos truthiness and copies sel.anchor/sel.focus/sel.tableCellRange verbatim (line 257); editor.ts:3614-3617 setPeerCursors assigns without validation. I searched repo-wide for a validator under other names (isDocPosition|isDocRange|toDocRange|coerceSelection|sanitizeSelection|sanitizePresence|validSelection|isValidRange → zero matches) and for object type-guards in packages/docs/src (only numeric-attrs.ts:287, clipboard.ts:74, editor.ts:3514, text-box-editor.ts:1069, none on this path); peer-cursor.ts has cycle guards but no shape guard. The throw path is real: editor.ts:2095 dereferences peer.selection.anchor.blockId, and for a valid anchor/focus with a malformed tableCellRange the throw lands in normalizeRange (selection.ts:181-195) → normalizeCellRange:139. Neither paint() (editor.ts:1900) nor render()/renderPaintOnly() (editor.ts:2395-2403) has a try/catch — the only try blocks in editor.ts are at 1343, 4120, 4159, 4166, 4172, 4185, none wrapping paint — so the persisted presence re-throws on every repaint, freezing the canvas for every other participant. In-lane as unsafe handling of untrusted cross-client input with cross-user availability impact, aggravated by presence writes not being permission-gated server-side (the app's own readOnly checks at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1444/3463 are client-side only, so a raw client, including a share-link viewer, bypasses them).

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:132-147) clamps only indices (clampCellIndex, 106-109) against `table.rows.length - 1` and a per-call `reduce` over every row for maxCol (136-137), then calls `expandCellRangeForMerges` at line 146 with no area or pass-count bound. That helper (56-98) is a `while (changed)` fixed point re-scanning the full rectangle each pass and invoking the O(area) `findMergeTopLeft` (33-45) for covered cells, so a staircase of rowSpan merges yields work superlinear in the peer-authored table size. It is reached from peer presence once per peer per paint at editor.ts:2098 (the only preceding guard, isRangeVisible at 2095, checks anchor/focus block ids, not the rectangle area) and for the local selection via getSelectionRects (812-820). Row count is genuinely unbanded: MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS (numeric-attrs.ts:95) caps columns, normalizeTableSpan caps spans (213-219), MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH caps nesting (yorkie-doc-store.ts:479-484), but no cap exists on rows.length on any read path (yorkie-doc-store.ts:436-443; numeric-attrs.ts:383-412). Line 189-191 additionally routes nested tables into the expansion via resolveNestedTableLayout, as the finding states. No guard renders it unreachable, and the repo's own comments (selection.ts:114-127, numeric-attrs.ts:205-211) classify peer-written unbounded render-path loops as the security hazard these bands close, so it is in-lane untrusted-input resource exhaustion.

finding.summary: The cycle-guard sweep missed two recursive parent-map walks: `moveToNextCell` / `moveToPrevCell` recurse through `blockParentMap` with no visited set
finding.evidence: This PR adds `seen` guards to six walks over `blockParentMap` on the stated threat model that a peer can write two tables whose ids make the parent chain loop (ids come verbatim from CRDT attributes; the map is built in table-layout.ts:451 keyed on those ids, so duplicate ids across two tables produce A→B and B→A). Two walks over the same map were left unguarded: `moveToNextCell` recurses at text-editor.ts:6007 after moving the caret into the parent cell, and `moveToPrevCell` at text-editor.ts:6065 does the same. With a cyclic map, Tab / Shift+Tab at a table boundary ping-pongs between the two tables until the stack overflows (RangeError out of the key handler) — the same crash the PR closes in `Doc.findBlockInCells`. Confidence is low because the Tab path may pass `addRowAtEnd`, which takes the insert-row branch before the exit branch on the last cell; Shift+Tab (`moveToPrevCell`) has no such branch.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed: moveToNextCell recurses at text-editor.ts:6007 and moveToPrevCell at text-editor.ts:6065, both after reading blockParentMap (text-editor.ts:5992, :6052), with no visited set or depth cap. Both are reachable from untrusted-input-driven UI paths: handleTab (text-editor.ts:2726-2734) and arrow handling (:3063, :3088). The cycle threat model is the repository's own: table-layout.ts:451 keys the map verbatim on peer-written block ids, and the parallel walks carry explicit `seen` guards with comments naming peer-written CRDT ids as the reason (table-layout.ts:503-518, text-editor.ts:3894-3906, :3919-3925). No dedupe/validation of ids exists before the map is built, and MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH bounds only structural layout recursion, not cross-table A->B/B->A map entries, so `already-guarded` does not hold. Remote-controlled unbounded recursion (stack overflow from the key handler) is untrusted-input handling in the security lane; severity major as impact. I could not build a full end-to-end exploit (each recursion hop must re-hit the last-cell branch), but uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: Peer-supplied `tableCellRange` row/col indices are never validated, so a remote peer's presence can drive unbounded render-path loops (tab hang) — the same DoS class the cycle guards in this delta close, through a field they do not cover
finding.evidence: Attack: any client attached to the doc (presence is writable even by a read-only viewer) publishes `activeSelection = { anchor: <any real block id>, focus: <same>, tableCellRange: { blockId: <a real table block id>, start: {rowIndex:0,colIndex:0}, end: {rowIndex:1e9,colIndex:1e9} } }`. `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:257` copies `sel.tableCellRange` verbatim into `PeerCursor.selection` with no bounds check, and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2098` feeds it to `computeSelectionRects` on every paint (the `isRangeVisible` gate at editor.ts:2095 only looks at anchor/focus blockIds, and returns `true` for unknown ids). From there: (a) `normalizeRange` -> `normalizeCellRange` -> `expandCellRangeForMerges` (selection.ts:68-90) iterates `for (r = rowStart; r <= rowEnd; r++) for (c = colStart; c <= colEnd; c++)` over the attacker's 1e9 x 1e9 rectangle, and (b) `buildCellRangeRects` (selection.ts:685-704) runs the identical double loop. JSON presence can also carry `1e400`, which parses to `Infinity`, making `r <= rowEnd` never false — a permanently wedged tab for every other collaborator, from one presence write. Note the codebase already recognises this exact sink: `normalizeTableSpan`'s doc comment (model/numeric-attrs.ts:205-211) bands `rowSpan` precisely because `expandCellRangeForMerges` is non-terminating on unbounded values — but the *range endpoints* themselves, which reach the same loop, get no equivalent band on the peer-presence path. This code is outside the delta, but it is the remaining open door in the very threat model the delta's guards are written against.

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise — that peer-supplied `tableCellRange` indices are "never validated" before reaching the render-path double loops — is not true of this repository. `clampCellIndex` (selection.ts:106-109) maps non-finite values (e.g. `1e400` -> `Infinity`) to 0 and truncs/clamps finite values into `[0, max]`. `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:132-147) applies it to both endpoints against the resolved table's row/column counts BEFORE calling `expandCellRangeForMerges` at line 146, and only calls the expander when a table resolved — so sink (a) never sees `1e9`/`Infinity`. The peer path necessarily goes through it: editor.ts:2098 -> computeSelectionRects (selection.ts:612) -> normalizeRange (selection.ts:176), whose tableCellRange branch returns `normalizeCellRange(...)` at line 195, and only then calls buildCellRangeRects at line 624. Sink (b) is independently bounded: buildCellRangeRects clamps its own loop bounds to the resolved layout table at selection.ts:725-728 (`Math.min(end.rowIndex, tl.cells.length - 1)`, `Math.min(end.colIndex, tl.columnXOffsets.length - 1)`, starts floored at 0) and returns [] at line 648 when the table does not resolve; the loop at 730-731 therefore cannot exceed the real table. The quoted evidence line numbers are also wrong (selection.ts:685-704 is the nested-fragment overlap loop, not the range loop). The copy sink `getSelectedText` (selection.ts:822-850) reads the same clamped range and bails at line 836. The other buildCellRangeRects call site (selection.ts:519-524) builds its range from local tableData dimensions.

finding.summary: No nesting-depth cap on the CRDT read path for nested tables (`treeNodeToBlock` -> `treeNodeToRow` -> `treeNodeToCell` -> `treeNodeToBlock`), nor on `computeTableLayout`/`layoutCellBlocks` — a peer-written deep nesting chain overflows the stack for every reader
finding.evidence: Vector: a peer writes a table nested inside a cell, repeated to a few tens of thousands of levels (pure CRDT node writes, no UI needed). `treeNodeToBlock` (crdt-tree.ts:213-243) recurses through rows/cells back into itself with no depth parameter, and `computeTableLayout` <-> `layoutCellBlocks` (view/table-layout.ts:133) mutually recurse once per nesting level, so `read()` or the first layout throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on every reader that opens the document. The repo already treats this as a real hazard on the other two ingest paths and caps them — clipboard paste at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (view/clipboard.ts:71,308) and attribute banding at `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` (model/numeric-attrs.ts:111,408, whose comment says explicitly 'a chain a peer can write to any depth — so an uncapped walk blows the stack') — but `bandBlockNumerics` only stops *descending* at 32, it does not truncate the content, so the layout recursion below it is still unbounded. I did not build a live repro, hence low confidence; the missing cap is visible in the code. Out of the delta, same untrusted-peer-data threat model.

verdict.reason: Both caps the finding claims are absent exist in the working tree, under the name MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26) rather than the MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH/MAX_NESTING names the reviewer grepped for. (1) CRDT read path: treeNodeToBlock(node, depth = 0) at crdt-tree.ts:219 returns rows = [] when depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (:225), otherwise recursing via treeNodeToRow(c, depth + 1) (:229); depth threads through treeNodeToRow (:201,205) and treeNodeToCell (:173,177), bounding the whole block>row>cell>block cycle. (2) Layout: layoutCellBlocks takes nestingDepth = 0 (table-layout.ts:118) and guards at :145 with `if (nestingDepth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)`, pushing one empty line instead of recursing; otherwise it calls computeTableLayout(..., nestingDepth + 1) (:161), which accepts nestingDepth (:241) and passes it back down (:285), closing the mutual recursion. Both guards sit inside the exact line ranges the reviewer says they read. The frontend "live twin" reader is capped identically (yorkie-doc-store.ts:57,480), the constant is exported for reuse (index.ts:97), and test/model/table-nesting.test.ts:63-65 exercises a 50,000-level chain asserting truncation at the cap. The supporting claim that the layout below bandBlockNumerics is "still unbounded" is false given table-layout.ts:145.

finding.summary: `resolvePositionPixel` walks the same parent map with an unguarded `while (true)` — and it is driven once per remote peer cursor per render
finding.evidence: peer-cursor.ts:121-127 is the identical walk the diff hardened elsewhere (`let currentTableId = cellInfo.tableBlockId; while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) with no `seen` set. Worse than the guarded sites, a cycle here also grows `nestingPath` without bound, so it is an unbounded allocation as well as an infinite loop — a memory-exhaustion/hang of every viewer, not only of a user who selects cells. This is the path that renders *peer* cursors, i.e. the one most directly fed by remote state, which is precisely the attacker the diff's own comment names. Not changed by this diff, but it is the sibling that makes the newly added guards incomplete.

verdict.reason: The finding claims resolvePositionPixel walks blockParentMap with an unguarded `while (true)` and no `seen` set. Reading the file directly, the guard is present: peer-cursor.ts:128 initializes `const seenTableIds = new Set<string>([currentTableId])`, line 132 checks `if (seenTableIds.has(parentInfo.tableBlockId)) return undefined;` BEFORE the `nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo)` on line 133, and line 135 adds each new id. This bounds both the loop iterations and `nestingPath` growth by the number of distinct ids in the map, closing both claimed impacts (infinite spin and unbounded allocation). Lines 122-127, which the finding quotes as the vulnerable code, are in fact the explanatory comment for that guard and explicitly name the peer-written-CRDT attacker. The sibling walks are guarded too (table-layout.ts:499-545, selection.ts:150-170 with the matching comment at :125). The reviewer's reported empty greps do not hold: `blockParentMap` appears at peer-cursor.ts:114 and :130. One concrete counterexample is enough here, and it is the exact line the finding says is missing.
